speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with respiratory distress; can you tell me exactly when these symptoms started and if there were any complications during the birth?

REQUEST TEST: Pulse_Oximetry
REQUEST TEST: Arterial_Blood_Gas

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Pulse Oximetry: 88% on room air, improving with oxygen; Arterial Blood Gas: pH 7.30 (slightly acidic), PaCO2 50 mm Hg (elevated), PaO2 60 mm Hg (reduced), HCO3- 24 mEq/L, Base Excess -5

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born after the 32nd gestational week. The baby was born via cesarean delivery. The mother had gestational diabetes but was otherwise healthy with no other pregnancy-related diseases.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Tachypnea, Subcostal and intercostal retractions, Nasal flaring, Cyanosis. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Urinary tract infection and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is an unusual presentation for a urinary tract infection; those signs strongly suggest a primary respiratory pathology like Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS) or Pneumonia. While I will wait for the Pulse Oximetry and Arterial Blood Gas results, can you tell me if your mother had a history of diabetes or if you were delivered prematurely?

REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray
REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Chest X-Ray: Findings indicate a ground-glass appearance with air bronchograms, suggestive of Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS).

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS) secondary to prematurity. The clinical signs of tachypnea, retractions, and nasal flaring, combined with the characteristic "ground-glass" appearance with air bronchograms on the Chest X-Ray, confirm this diagnosis.
